Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 65, English)
Atoms, Prana Urja, and the Shiv Tattva: Why the Smallest Thing Is Actually the Biggest

Sour ce: A live, interactive teaching session (opening with an attendee r oll call), continuing dir ectly from a prior video on Dimensions and mantra. This document is Part I of III — Knowledge Base, Q&A Pairs, and Curated Conversational Q&A.

1. Session framing: starting fr om the smallest measurable thing. Per this teaching, since the lar gest thing in existence cannot be measured or grasped, Bhaiya instead chooses to start from the smallest — the atom — as the entry point for this session's teaching.

2. Basic atomic structur e, as the starting r eference point. Per this teaching, an atom has a nucleus containing protons and neutrons, with electrons orbiting around it — introduced deliberately as familiar , conventional science before being reinterpreted spiritually .

3. Recap: the Yaksha Shlok energy mechanism (fr om a prior video). Per this teaching, referencing an earlier explanation: solar ener gy reflects through a lar ge "Om" symbol; simultaneously , meditation ener gy from saints is directed through a glass panel; the two meet at a cross-section point, forming a spherical, beam-shaped emission that falls onto the Earth as prana urja (life-force ener gy), which develops/grows whatever element it lands on and connects to.

4. Cor e question raised: why doesn't the electr on collapse into the pr oton? Per this teaching, since protons (positive) and electrons (negative) attract each other , conventional physics would predict the electron should eventually collapse into the nucleus — yet it does not. Ordinary science does not fully explain why; this teaching proposes prana urja as the missing piece of the explanation.

5. The electron's continuous motion r equires a continuous outside for ce. Per this teaching, applying Newton's First Law (an object's natural tendency is toward rest/inertia unless a force acts on it), the electron's motion should eventually slow and stop due to some form of friction/resistance — but it never does. This is of fered as evidence that some continuous, unseen force/ener gy is being supplied to sustain it.

6. The repulsion for ce between proton and electr on also r equires ongoing energy . Per this teaching, when an electron approaches too close to the proton, a repulsion force activates to keep them apart — and this repulsion force, too, is described as requiring a continuous ener gy supply of its own.

7. Why both particles r emaining externally neutral is itself significant. Per this teaching, if protons and electrons were not externally neutral, they would become char ged and release ener gy uncontrollably — the fact that this equilibrium is maintained continuously , without collapsing into instability , is presented as further evidence of an underlying, continuously supplied ener gy source (referenced alongside phenomena like atomic bombs and boson/"God particle" collision experiments as further illustrations that such ener gy exists and can be released).

8. This pattern is universal acr oss all atoms on Earth. Per this teaching, every atom on Earth — with electrons, protons, and neutrons — maintains this same externally neutral, continuously active state, running without interruption, 24 hours a day , 7 days a week.

9. Cosmic-scale motion (galaxy r otation, Earth's orbital speed) is cited as further evidence against pur e randomness. Per this teaching, the fact that the galaxy and Earth move at specific, consistent speeds (referenced approximately as galaxy rotation speed and Earth's roughly 29 km/second orbital speed) is of fered as evidence that this is not random chance but a maintained, symmetric system — since true randomness would not sustain this level of ongoing structure and precision.

10. Using drishti to look "inside" a pr oton or electron. Per this teaching, using subtle sight (drishti) to magnify and look progressively deeper inside a proton or electron reveals, in sequence: tiny , insect-like beings/forms in various postures, moving; then a strange white fluid; then something resembling a vibrating string (echoing string theory); and finally , "matter" itself.

1 1. What happens when two units of "matter" collide. Per this teaching, when one unit of matter collides ("collapses") with another matter of the same underlying type, a spark occurs — and this spark/current, arising specifically from this collision within deep, dark subtle matter , is what this teaching identifies as "Shiv ."

12. How a white fluid, and eventually life itself, forms fr om this pr ocess. Per this teaching, when many such elemental sparks/collisions accumulate, they form a white fluid, within which life begins to form, and within that life, hundreds of further distinct elements form in turn.

13. This "dark matter ," perceived via drishti, is identified with Shiv Tattva. Per this teaching, what is perceived through drishti as this deep, dark subtle matter is identified as the Shiv Tattva — described as something that pervades and "prevails" everywhere, in every location.

14. An important distinction: this natural "Shiv" spark is differ ent from the specific "Shiv Tattva" vessel cr eated and distributed by Bholenath (Shankar). Per this teaching, Bhaiya draws a deliberate distinction: the naturally occurring spark/current arising from matter -collision (described above) is one thing; separately , the specific person known as Shankar (Bholenath) is described as having taken prana urja from above, created his own distinct ener gy "bowl" (katora), and distributed it below so that people could draw their own shakti from that base — it is this specific, deliberately created and distributed vessel that is typically referred to in teaching as "Shiv Tattva." Bhaiya poses this as an open question for reflection: are these two "Shiv" concepts the same, or genuinely dif ferent?

15. "Mahadev" as a further -intensified form of this same dark matter . Per this teaching, Mahadev is described as this same dark matter taken to an even greater ("maha") intensity — Bhaiya leaves it as an open reflective question whether this should be understood as literal "shunya" (zero/void) or as "mahasookshma" (an extremely subtle, near -infinitesimal state), since true zero cannot exist if sparks are still occurring within it.

16. The central paradox of this session: the smallest thing is actually the biggest. Per this teaching, this is presented as a key , repeatedly emphasized insight: "jo jitna zyada chhota hai, wo utna hi bada hai" (the smaller something is, the bigger it actually is) — of fered as a principle to hold onto while working through the rest of this teaching.

17. What mantra actually does, mechanically , in this framework. Per this teaching, a suf ficiently subtle mantra, as it descends through successive Dimensions (2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, and onward), eventually reaches the level of this same dark-matter/spark phenomenon — enabling the practitioner to witness the underlying shakti at work, and ultimately , at a suf ficiently deep Dimension (described here as around the 10th Dimension), to directly witness Bhagwan Shiv himself.

18. Beyond Shiv: the still-undiscover ed higher Dimensions, Vaikunth, and Ram Tattva. Per this teaching, historic sant literature describes the 14th Dimension as corresponding to Vaikunth — but, per Bhaiya, no direct proof or witnessed confirmation of Vaikunth exists yet through this specific method; only the Shiv Tattva has actually been "found"/witnessed so far via this particular mantra-based descent into the sookshma (subtle/quantum) world. Ram Tattva , associated with Saket Dham (described in scripture as situated even above Vaikunth, at the very top), is explicitly described as "yet to be discover ed" by this method.

19. Refer ence to "four corners and 14 bhavans (lokas)." Per this teaching, referencing traditional cosmology describing four directional corners and 14 total lokas/realms, with the topmost and final loka being Saket — illustrated with a lighthearted comparison

to the idea that if someone already lives at the top ("Saket" of a city , jokingly compared to a Delhi neighborhood of the same name), there is nothing higher above them, and they should make way for others.

20. Why becoming mor e "sookshma" (subtle) can also mean fragmenting oneself. Per this teaching, as a practitioner becomes progressively more subtle in their practice, they are, in a sense, dividing themselves and their own mantra into smaller pieces (rather than remaining a single unified whole) — of fered as a nuanced caution alongside the "smaller is bigger" principle, not a contradiction of it.

21. The direct equivalence drawn between "sookshma jagat" and the "quantum world." Per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly equates the traditional term "sookshma jagat" (subtle world) with the modern scientific term "quantum world" — of fering this direct translation specifically to help practitioners map this teaching onto familiar scientific vocabulary .

22. This session explicitly builds on, and should be combined with, material fr om a pr evious session's teaching. Per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly instructs practitioners to mentally combine what was taught in this session with what was taught in an immediately preceding session (on Dimensions 1 through 8+ and mantra), since the two sessions together form one continuous, cumulative teaching arc.

23. Practical caution: choose an alr eady-subtle mantra rather than trying to make an ordinary mantra mor e subtle over time. Per this teaching, a mantra can, in principle, be taken to any degree of subtlety a practitioner wishes — but the recommended approach is to start with a mantra that is alr eady very subtle, rather than starting with a denser/heavier mantra and attempting to progressively refine it. Per this teaching, if a practitioner keeps "magnifying"/refining a mantra that began dense, at some point it will inevitably "fall" — and there is a real risk that this fall could land back upon the practitioner themself.

24. Why older , mor e established deities and mantras ar e described as mor e powerful. Per this teaching, the mantras used for genuinely "awakened" (jagrit) practice are not modern, Kalyug-era inventions — as a general principle, the older a given deity is, the more mantra jaap has been directed toward that deity cumulatively , across history , by practitioners over time, and this cumulative history of jaap is what makes an older deity's tattva more powerful.

25. A real-world example discussed: a public figur e's "Surya Kaksha" (Surya Class) practice and its r esults. Per this teaching, in response to a sangat member's question about a public figure ("Karim Khan") whose own spiritual journey reportedly began after being guided by another teacher ("Manu Bhaiya") into a "Surya Kaksha" (Sun-focused practice), Bhaiya explains that many people's cumulative jaap toward that same Surya Kala practice would indeed have helped elevate that person's own Dimension — but notes that this particular person is not yet visible within the sookshma jagat (subtle/quantum world) through this specific lens. Bhaiya attributes that individual's overall progress primarily to merit carried over from a past life ("purv janam ki hai"), rather than solely to this-lifetime practice, and notes that although this person has since diver ged onto a separate spiritual path with dif ferent specific practices, this is not viewed negatively — Bhaiya explicitly states such an individual continues to act with good intent and does not cause harm to others, even while following a dif ferent specific lineage or method.

26. Differ ent gurus/lineages naturally have differ ent specific mantra practices — but the underlying destination is described as the same. Per this teaching, guru paddhati (a guru's specific method), parampara (lineage/tradition), and niyam (rules/practices) legitimately dif fer from one lineage to another , resulting in dif ferent specific techniques across dif ferent teachers — but this is compared to the many dif ferent routes one can take to reach the same city (Delhi): the specific path dif fers, but the ultimate destination — described here as reaching "Saket," i.e., the highest realm — remains the same regardless of which specific lineage's method a practitioner follows.

27. The neutron's specific function within the sookshma jagat (subtle world), described as a "buffer solution." Per this teaching, in response to a sangat member's own observation, the neutron is described as functioning like a stable, self-contained entity — comparable to a chemistry "buf fer solution" — that has its own internal cycle and specifically works to draw in or absorb elements/tattvas that have become excessively/extremely char ged, helping to maintain overall balance within the system.

28. The distinction between the form (sakar) commonly worshipped as "Shiv" and the true formless (nirakar) Shiv . Per this teaching, the personified Shiv form that practitioners commonly visualize or see in meditation/vision is explicitly described as dif ferent from the true, underlying Shiv — described as "jo hoke bhi nahi hai" (that which exists and yet does not exist/has no fixed form), i.e., genuinely nirakar (formless), with no fixed shape at all. Per this teaching, this is specifically why the Shivling (an abstract, nonanthropomorphic symbol) — rather than a humanoid murti/form — is the traditional object of worship for Shiv: because the true Shiv tattva itself has no form to depict.

29. The Om/turiya-state connection to this nirakar (formless) principle. Per this teaching, this formless aspect is connected to the concept of turiya avastha (the fourth, transcendent state of consciousness) and to the phrase "Omkar moolam" (Om as the root/source) — with Om itself described as representing precisely this nirakar dimension of Shiv , distinct from any specific personified form (such as Bhairav or other associated deities) that a practitioner might otherwise worship in sakar (form-based) devotion.

30. Clarifying this session's actual goal: understanding the universe, not seeking nirakar realization for its own sake. Per this teaching, Bhaiya is explicit that whichever specific deity or form (sakar) a practitioner already worships remains entirely valid and does not need to change — the purpose of this particular teaching is not to push practitioners toward nirakar (formless) worship or realization as a goal in itself. As Bhaiya states directly: "hum sirf apne universe ko samajh rahe hain" (we are simply trying to understand our own universe) — and, per this teaching, this understanding itself is the entire point of walking through this material, with no further goal beyond it.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session starts from the atom (protons, neutrons, electrons) as the smallest measurable reference point, since the lar gest thing in existence cannot be directly measured. The electron's continued orbit, the proton-electron repulsion force, and the maintained external neutrality of both particles are each of fered as evidence of a continuous, unseen ener gy supply (prana urja) sustaining ordinary matter — not fully explained by conventional science alone. Using drishti to look progressively deeper inside a proton/electron reveals, in sequence: tiny moving forms, a white fluid, a vibrating "string," and finally "matter" itself; when two units of this matter collide, the resulting spark is identified as "Shiv ." This naturally occurring "Shiv" spark (arising from matter -collision) is explicitly distinguished from the specific "Shiv Tattva" vessel that Bholenath (Shankar) is described as having personally created and distributed for people to draw shakti from — these are presented as two related but distinct concepts. Central teaching: "the smaller something is, the bigger it actually is" — held alongside the caution that becoming more subtle can also mean fragmenting oneself and one's own mantra. Mantra descends through successive Dimensions and, at a suf ficiently deep level (around the 10th Dimension in this framework), can lead to direct witnessing of Bhagwan Shiv — but Vaikunth (traditionally the 14th Dimension) and Ram Tattva (associated with Saket Dham, above Vaikunth) remain explicitly undiscovered/unproven by this specific method so far . "Sookshma jagat" (the subtle world) is explicitly equated with the modern scientific "quantum world." This session should be understood as continuing directly from, and combined with, the material taught in the immediately preceding Dimensions/mantra session. Choose an already-subtle mantra rather than refining a dense one over time — repeatedly "magnifying" a mantra that began dense risks it eventually "falling," potentially back onto the practitioner; older , longer -worshipped deities and mantras are described as more powerful precisely because of the cumulative jaap directed at them across history . Different gurus/lineages have dif ferent specific methods and practices, but the ultimate destination (Saket) is the same regardless of path, much like dif ferent routes to the same city . The neutron functions like a stable "buf fer solution" within the sookshma jagat, absorbing excessively char ged elements to maintain balance.

The commonly worshipped, personified form of Shiv is explicitly distinguished from the true, formless (nirakar) Shiv — which is why the abstract Shivling, rather than a humanoid form, is the traditional object of worship; this connects to turiya avastha and "Omkar moolam." This teaching's actual goal is explicitly stated as understanding the universe itself, not pursuing nirakar realization as an end in itself — any practitioner's existing sakar (form-based) devotion remains fully valid and does not need to change. This session included genuine live interaction (roll call, playful exchanges, and audience engagement), so Part III (Curated Conversational Q&A) is included for this session. Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 65, English)
Atoms, Prana Urja, and the Shiv Tattva: Why the Smallest Thing Is Actually the Biggest
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live training session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siyaram."

Q1. Why does this session start with the atom rather than something larger? A: Per this teaching, since the lar gest thing in existence cannot be measured or grasped, Bhaiya deliberately starts from the smallest measurable reference point instead — the atom.

Q2. According to conventional physics, why should an electr on eventually collapse into the pr oton, and why doesn't it? A: Per this teaching, since protons (positive) and electrons (negative) attract each other , conventional physics would predict eventual collapse — yet it never happens; this teaching proposes that a continuous, unseen prana urja (life-force ener gy) is what actually sustains the electron's stable orbit, something ordinary science does not fully explain.

Q3. What does Newton's First Law have to do with why the electr on keeps moving? A: Per this teaching, Newton's First Law implies that without a continuous force, motion should eventually slow and stop due to friction/resistance — since the electron's motion never stops, this is of fered as evidence that some continuous, unseen ener gy is being supplied to sustain it.

Q4. Does the r epulsion for ce between proton and electr on also need energy? A: Yes — per this teaching, the repulsion force that activates when an electron gets too close to the proton is described as also requiring its own continuous ener gy supply to keep functioning.

Q5. Why does it matter that pr otons and electr ons r emain externally neutral? A: Per this teaching, if they weren't neutral, they would become char ged and release ener gy uncontrollably — the fact that this neutral equilibrium is maintained continuously is presented as further evidence of an underlying, continuously supplied ener gy source.

Q6. Is this pattern unique to certain atoms, or universal? A: Per this teaching, it is universal — every atom on Earth maintains this same externally neutral, continuously active state, running without interruption, 24/7.

Q7. What does Earth's orbital speed have to do with this teaching? A: Per this teaching, the fact that the galaxy and Earth move at specific, consistent speeds (Earth's orbital speed referenced at roughly 29 km/second) is of fered as evidence against pure randomness — true randomness would not sustain this level of ongoing structure and precision.

Q8. What does drishti r eveal when looking pr ogr essively deeper inside a pr oton or electron? A: Per this teaching, magnifying inward reveals, in sequence: tiny , insect-like moving forms, then a strange white fluid, then something resembling a vibrating string, and finally "matter" itself.

Q9. What happens, per this teaching, when two units of this "matter" collide? A: Per this teaching, a spark occurs, and this spark/current — arising specifically from collision within deep, dark subtle matter — is identified as "Shiv ."

Q10. How does life eventually form fr om this pr ocess, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, when many such elemental sparks/collisions accumulate, they form a white fluid, within which life begins to form, and within that life, hundreds of further distinct elements form in turn.

Q1 1. Is the "Shiv" spark fr om matter -collision the same as the "Shiv Tattva" commonly r eferenced in earlier sessions? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly distinguishes the two: the naturally occurring spark from matter -collision is one thing, while the specific "Shiv Tattva" vessel commonly referenced in teaching is described as something Bholenath (Shankar) personally created — taking prana urja from above, forming his own distinct ener gy "bowl," and distributing it below for people to draw shakti from. Bhaiya poses whether these are the same or dif ferent as an open question for reflection, rather than giving a single definitive answer .

Q12. What is "Mahadev ," in relation to this teaching's dark-matter framework? A: Per this teaching, Mahadev is described as this same dark matter taken to an even greater ("maha") intensity — left as an open question whether this should be understood as literal "shunya" (zero/void) or as "mahasookshma" (an extremely subtle, near -infinitesimal state).

Q13. What is the central paradox emphasized in this session? A: Per this teaching, it is this: "the smaller something is, the bigger it actually is" — presented as a key insight to hold onto throughout the rest of the teaching.

Q14. What does mantra actually do, mechanically , in this framework? A: Per this teaching, a suf ficiently subtle mantra descends through successive Dimensions, eventually reaching the level of the dark-matter/spark phenomenon described in this session — allowing the practitioner to witness the underlying shakti at work, and at a suf ficiently deep Dimension (around the 10th, in this framework), to directly witness Bhagwan Shiv .

Q15. Has Vaikunth (traditionally the 14th Dimension) actually been witnessed or proven thr ough this method? A: No — per this teaching, historic sant literature places Vaikunth at the 14th Dimension, but Bhaiya is explicit that no direct proof or witnessed confirmation of Vaikunth exists yet through this specific mantra-based descent; only the Shiv Tattva has actually been found/witnessed so far .

Q16. Has Ram Tattva been discover ed through this method? A: No — per this teaching, Ram Tattva, associated with Saket Dham (described as situated even above Vaikunth), is explicitly described as "yet to be discovered" by this specific method.

Q17. What is the significance of "four corners and 14 bhavans (lokas)"? A: Per this teaching, this references traditional cosmology describing four directional corners and 14 total lokas/realms, with the topmost and final loka being Saket.

Q18. Does becoming mor e spiritually "subtle" (sookshma) have any downside, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, yes — as a practitioner becomes progressively more subtle, they are, in a sense, dividing themselves and their own mantra into smaller pieces rather than remaining a single unified whole; this is of fered as a nuanced caution alongside the "smaller is bigger" principle, not a contradiction of it.

Q19. What is the "sookshma jagat" (subtle world), in modern scientific terms? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly equates "sookshma jagat" directly with the modern scientific term "quantum world."

Q20. Should this session be understood on its own, or alongside another session? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly instructs practitioners to combine this session's material with what was taught in the immediately preceding session (on Dimensions and mantra), since the two form one continuous, cumulative teaching arc.

Q21. Should a practitioner take an ordinary mantra and try to make it mor e and mor e subtle over time? A: No — per this teaching, it's better to start with a mantra that is already very subtle; repeatedly "magnifying"/refining a mantra that began dense carries a real risk that it will eventually "fall," possibly back onto the practitioner themself.

Q22. Why ar e older deities and mantras described as mor e powerful? A: Per this teaching, the mantras used for genuinely awakened practice are not modern, Kalyug-era inventions — the older a deity is, the more cumulative jaap has been directed toward that deity across history , and this accumulated history of practice is what makes an older deity's tattva more powerful.

Q23. A sangat member asked about a public figur e whose journey began with a "Surya Kaksha" practice taught by another guide — did Bhaiya confirm this person's pr ogr ess? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya acknowledges that cumulative jaap toward that same Surya Kala practice by many people would indeed help elevate that person's Dimension, but notes the person is not yet visible

within the sookshma jagat through this specific lens — Bhaiya attributes their overall progress mainly to merit from a past life, and notes that although they've since followed a separate path, they continue to act with good intent and cause no harm to others.

Q24. If differ ent gurus teach differ ent specific mantra practices, does that mean they lead to differ ent outcomes? A: No — per this teaching, guru paddhati, parampara, and specific rules legitimately dif fer between lineages, but this is compared to dif ferent routes to the same city: the specific path dif fers, but the ultimate destination (Saket, the highest realm) remains the same.

Q25. What is the neutr on's specific r ole within the sookshma jagat (subtle world), per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, the neutron functions like a stable "buf fer solution" — a self-contained entity with its own internal cycle that specifically draws in and absorbs excessively/extremely char ged elements to help maintain overall balance.

Q26. Is the personified form of Shiv that people commonly visualize the same as the "true" Shiv? A: No — per this teaching, the commonly worshipped, personified Shiv form is explicitly distinguished from the true, underlying Shiv , described as genuinely formless (nirakar) — "that which exists and yet has no fixed form."

Q27. Why do practitioners worship the Shivling instead of a humanoid form of Shiv? A: Per this teaching, because the true Shiv tattva itself has no form to depict — the abstract Shivling, rather than an anthropomorphic murti, is the traditional object of worship precisely because Shiv is fundamentally nirakar (formless).

Q28. What do "turiya avastha" and "Omkar moolam" have to do with this formless aspect of Shiv? A: Per this teaching, turiya avastha (the fourth, transcendent state of consciousness) and the phrase "Omkar moolam" (Om as the root/source) both connect to this nirakar principle — Om itself is described as representing precisely this formless dimension of Shiv , distinct from any specific personified form a practitioner might otherwise worship.

Q29. Does this teaching mean practitioners should stop worshipping deities in their personified (sakar) form and pursue formless (nirakar) r ealization instead? A: No — per this teaching, Bhaiya is explicit that whichever form of worship a practitioner already practices remains entirely valid and does not need to change; the actual point of this teaching is simply to understand the universe itself ("hum sirf apne universe ko samajh rahe hain"), not to push practitioners toward nirakar realization as a goal in itself.

Keep the distinction between the naturally occurring "Shiv" spark (from matter -collision, witnessed via drishti) and the specific "Shiv Tattva" vessel attributed to Bholenath/Shankar intact and clearly separated — this session poses it as an open, reflective question rather than resolving it into one single claim. Keep the "smaller is bigger" paradox and its companion caution (subtlety can mean self-fragmentation) both intact, since this teaching presents them as complementary , not contradictory . Preserve the explicit "sookshma jagat = quantum world" equivalence exactly as stated, since this is of fered as a direct, deliberate translation for the practitioner's benefit. Note that this session explicitly builds on and should be read alongside the immediately preceding Dimensions/mantra session, when relevant context is needed. Do not name or speculate further about the specific public figure referenced regarding the "Surya Kaksha" practice beyond what is stated here — this teaching treats the example gently and without criticism, attributing their diver gent path to good intent and past-life merit rather than error .

Keep the sakar/nirakar (form/formless) distinction regarding Shiv precise: the commonly worshipped personified form and the true nirakar Shiv are explicitly described as dif ferent, and this is specifically why the Shivling (not a humanoid form) is the traditional object of worship — do not present this as a criticism of personified/sakar devotion generally , since the teaching explicitly af firms that any existing form of worship remains valid.
